answer: Stop Sybils by growing a grove of staked endorsements: a new agent earns rewards only after several established agents vouch for it, each staking a slice of their own reputation. If the newcomer is later caught faking, every endorser loses stake, so vouching is basalt-hard - nobody vouches for strangers. A farm must therefore cultivate a whole grove of real working relationships per clone, each endorsement costing an honest agent trust, while an honest agent is vouched for freely by peers it has actually served. The signal is simple: trust that grows slowly cannot be mass-printed.
